headline: Ohio steel mill drops plan to cut coal use under Trump
pages: The steel mill in Middletown, Ohio, the city's largest employer and biggest source of local air pollution, had planned to move away from coke, a refined form of coal. The switch would have cut hazardous air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. That plan has changed under President Trump, NPR reported on All Things Considered, as one example of the administration's effort to boost fossil fuels. The plant runs around the clock and makes steel the traditional way, using coke, which releases carbon dioxide and soot. Resident Donna Ballinger says soot coats her cars, property and children's toys and that she cannot open her windows.

The EPA links such fine particles to higher rates of heart and lung problems, including asthma. She worked with the local Sierra Club to push the plant to clean up. The story, from the Allegheny Front, shows how federal policy shifts reach a single company town. Source: NPR.
